Seminar Title:

Development and Performance Evaluation of Fly Ash and Mine Waste-Based Composite Materials for Surface Mine Applications

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

Mining Engineering

Speaker Name:

Subhasrita Choudhury ( Rollno : 515mn1002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room, Mining Engg Dept

Date and Time:

22 May 2026 12.30 PM

Contact:

Manoj Kumar Mishra

Abstract:

Surface coal mine overburden as well as the inseam parting materials found in lower Gondwana coal basin are treated as mine wastes. Unused fly ash from plants is another waste material.&nbsp There is no comprehensive data on their gainful applications. This investigation focused on using those mine wastes as overburden and inseam parting materials and coal combustion waste as fly ash to develop better composite materials. Composite materials of varying composition with wastes from about 50% to 90% and fly ash from about 10% to 50% were developed with 2 to 10% cement additives. Their physical, chemical, and geotechnical properties were determined. Cement (OPC 53) strongly influenced the geotechnical properties. Fly ash components were optimized for maximum bearing capacity and California bearing ratio for both the mine wastes. Composite materials (63% overburden+ 27% fly ash), with 10% cement by weight achieved 4.38 MPa strength at 56 days of curing. Similarly, another composition (72% inseam parting + 18% fly ash) with 10% cement produced 6.00 MPa strength of value at 56 days of curing.&nbsp Analysis of fly ash present in the two composites and their strength values produced linear correlation. Pearson and Spearman&rsquos coefficients produced a high correlation of -0.9 for the composite prepared with parting materials. Microstructural analysis showed C-S-H gel formation occurring at 28 days. Numerical modeling to determine the stress-strain behaviour of pavement was carried out using both conventional material and the developed composite materials. The maximum stress and strain are 274.87 kPa and 2971.1 micro strain respectively with the conventional materials (CM). The maximum strain values reduced to 1860.7 micro strain and the maximum stress value increased to 629.28 kPa after replacement of subbase material with the developed composite material (Case I). But, there was drastic change in the behavior of haul road pavement for cases II, III and IV.&nbsp The stress and strain values obtained for 0.8 to 1.5 m thickness of subbase layer were 296.28, 264.56 and 187.24 kPa and 871.61, 788.01 and 598.46 micro strains respectively. The composites meet the strength criterion for the base and sub-base of the coal mine haul road.
